n1: The node is bound to the right target and has full coverage, so avoid changing its scope or adding checks. The disagreement is semantic: the edited image clearly shows progress toward graphite/pencil styling (muted, near-grayscale tones and visible grain/texture), while retaining photographic shading and some color, especially in the tablecloth. Make the criteria distinguish partial progress from complete fulfillment using the requested medium as a whole-image rendering criterion; do not let desaturation or texture alone automatically count as complete, and do not treat remaining color as proof that no progress occurred. The traces are valid and queried with no dependency or transport failures, so this is not a schema issue. Because the reference is only an aggregate label and traces vary between complete and partial, refine the boundary and evidence guidance rather than hard-coding the reference label or treating repeated high confidence as ground truth.

The node is already well calibrated: all five valid, high-confidence traces agree on partial, and the edited image supports that judgment. Preserve the distinction between genuine partial progress and completion; do not treat muted color or grain alone as proof of a pencil-drawing transformation. The edited image is visibly desaturated and grainy, with some softened, sketch-like treatment, but the food, tableware, and background largely retain photographic shading and lack consistent pencil linework or tonal strokes. Preserve the distinction between genuine partial progress and completion: muted color or grain alone is not proof of pencil rendering, while residual photographic areas do not erase the visible progress.
